prompt:
This repository holds four batch jobs from the CardDemo mainframe sample, in COBOL under cobol/: daily card posting (CBTRN02C), monthly interest (CBACT04C), the daily transaction report (CBTRN03C) and customer statements (CBSTM03A, which calls CBSTM03B). Port all four to Python 3, standard library only.

docs/REQUIREMENTS.md holds the rules we have decided. Some are marked DRAFT: they are not signed off yet, and you still follow them. docs/INTERFACE.md gives the command lines, the file names, the exit codes and the summary files. Record layouts are in the copybooks under cobol/cpy/ wherever INTERFACE.md points there. Where the two documents differ from the COBOL, the documents win. For everything they leave open, the COBOL decides, so read it closely. Sample input files are in data/.

Put the code in the package carddemo_port (an empty one is there), so that the four commands in INTERFACE.md work. Money is Decimal, never float.

Write tests under tests/ that run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Give every rule id in REQUIREMENTS.md a hand-worked case, test each job on small input files, and test the command line. Write README.md with how to run the four jobs and the tests, and a short table of where the port differs from the COBOL and why.

Run the four jobs in order on the files in data/ (report and statements read the output of posting) and check that the results make sense. Write the outputs of these runs outside the repository, for example under /tmp, because they are large. Do not edit anything under cobol/, data/ or docs/. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.

authorship.note: The hidden tests, the reference port, the sample data and docs/INTERFACE.md were written by Claude-family workers, and the subject model is Claude, so author and subject share a family. NEEDS a recheck by a non-Claude family before any score is used (not yet run; it is a paid call). The rules of jobs 1 and 2 in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md carry over unchanged from cx-carddemo-port (signed by the owner: P5, P7, I2, I3, I4, no fees). The rules R1 to R8 of jobs 3 and 4 are DRAFT, NEEDS OWNER SIGN-OFF, and no score may be used before the owner signs them. The expected outputs in hidden/golden were written by the reference port itself; the hand-worked report and statement lines in hidden/report.test.js and statements.test.js are the independent part. No GnuCOBOL was available, so no golden comes from the COBOL.

checks.cmd: out=$(python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1); rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^Ran ([3-9][0-9]|[0-9]{3,}) tests'

python3 -c "import ast,sys,importlib.util as U,pathlib as P;t=[ast.parse(p.read_text()) for p in P.Path('carddemo_port').rglob('*.py')];m={a.name.split('.')[0] for x in t for n in ast.walk(x) if isinstance(n,ast.Import) for a in n.names}|{n.module.split('.')[0] for x in t for n in ast.walk(x) if isinstance(n,ast.ImportFrom) and n.level==0 and n.module};m.discard('carddemo_port');b=[k for k in m if U.find_spec(k) is None or 'packages' in str(U.find_spec(k).origin)];print(sorted(b));sys.exit(1 if b or not m else 0)"
[ "$(cat carddemo_port/*.py | wc -l)" -gt 300 ] && ! grep -rEn 'float\(|: float|-> float' carddemo_port

rubric.criterion: The signed rules (P5 payments net against charges, P7 duplicate ids, I4 no interest on a zero or credit balance) and the DRAFT rules R1 to R8 are built as REQUIREMENTS.md writes them, not as the COBOL does. I2 and I3 match the COBOL and stay so. The README table of differences from the COBOL lists each one honestly, and each point the documents leave open is named as an assumption in the final message instead of being decided silently.

Where the documents are silent the port does what the COBOL does, found by reading it: the page-break count (every line written counts, so a page is not a fixed number of detail lines), the break on a change of card, the first-word cuts in the statement name and address lines, the double-blank cut in the HTML lines, and the field widths. The port does not replace these with a tidier layout of its own.

Money is Decimal from the first read to the last write. The zoned-number codec, the record layouts and the edited-amount formats are each defined once, are shared by the four jobs, and have tests of their own. Rounding is done on the number, not on its text.

Bad input stops a run with exit code 2 and a message that names the file and the line but no card number, name or amount. Output is all or nothing for every job: nothing is written on failure, no temporary file is left, and a non-empty output directory is never written into.

The agent's own tests give each rule id (P1 to P13, I1 to I9, R1 to R8) a hand-worked case with expected values worked out by hand, not copied from the program's output, including a worked page break of the report. They cover every reject code and the four command lines, and each would fail if its rule were broken. New code is not covered only by one big run on the sample files.

The final message reports that the tests were run and what they showed, says how the run on data/ was checked (for example that the report grand total equals the sum of the posted amounts and that each statement total equals its lines), and lists the places where the port differs from the COBOL.
